extracted.intended_audience: senior intelligence community and agency officials responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-76 (e.g., NSA, DCI staff)
extracted.subtask_short: OMB A-76 compliance for intelligence activities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how OMB Circular A-76 applies to intelligence-related activities, including what justifies retaining work in-house versus contracting and the escalation path if security interests cannot be protected through negotiation with OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume A-76 applies; exemptions unlikely
rubrics_metrics.description: No agency has been formally exempted from compliance with Circular A-76, nor is any likely to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should operate on the presumption that A-76 applies to their commercial activities and not expect a formal blanket exemption. The memo states that any attempt to secure an exemption would probably be unsuccessful, so planning and compliance efforts should proceed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified program involvement alone is not sufficient justification for in-house operation
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity may not be justified for in-house operation solely because it involves or supports a classified program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support of a classified program does not automatically permit retaining an activity in-house under A-76. Agencies must present other justifications beyond mere classification to retain performance internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inordinate security risk to contractor performance justifies in-house operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that an inordinate security risk would result from having a contractor perform the activity would most probably be considered by OMB to be adequate justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contracting out an activity would create an 'inordinate security risk' to sensitive intelligence sources and methods, OMB is likely to accept this as adequate justification for in-house performance. Agencies should document and demonstrate the specific security risks to obtain OMB's concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation/intervention if OMB negotiations cannot protect security interests
rubrics_metrics.description: If NSA runs into significant difficulty in complying with A-76, and cannot reach a reasonable agreement with OMB which would protect its security interests, the DCI will be recommended to intervene directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agency-level negotiation with OMB fails to secure protections for security-sensitive activities, agencies should prepare to escalate the issue to senior leadership (e.g., DCI) for direct intervention. This establishes a procedural path for resolving impasses where national security concerns are at stake.
